evidence.quote: | Ok [ "borrow"; m; c ] -> UseCases.borrow ports m c |> render showBorrow

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The blocking rule for borrow, hold and renew is decided in Tier 2: Accounts.ensureNotBlocked is called inside Loans.borrow, Holds.place and Loans.renew, and renew runs it before the DEC-004 reasons. Tier 3 views (members, standing) ask Accounts.isBlocked and Accounts.owed and do not re-derive the rule. The change also removes the old CLI-side fines-minus-payments >= 5.00m check, so Tier 4 no longer decides anything. The CLI only branches on the Tier 3 view's Blocked flag to pick the output text.

evidence.quote: let renew ports (copyId: string) : Result<Views.RenewView, LendingError> =
| Ok [ "renew"; c ] -> UseCases.renew ports c |> render showRenew

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effect is added below Tier 4. The new standing and renew use cases go through the existing commit/query helpers, which use the Store and Clock ports. The change removes the existing places where the CLI called ports.Store.Load()/Save and ports.Clock() directly and called Loans.renew (Tier 2) itself. Everything now goes through UseCases, so the Tier 2 decision logic stays pure.

evidence.quote: blocked until it is below {money Policy.blockingBalance}

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The blocking balance has one definition, Policy.blockingBalance. The guard, isBlocked and the refusal message all reference it. The change removes the CLI's duplicated 5.00m literal and its own fines-minus-payments derivation; what a member owes now comes only from Accounts.owed.

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The per-member-type balance is decided in Tier 2 (the Policy.blockingBalance match on memberType, used by Accounts.isBlocked and ensureNotBlocked). Tier 3 views only pass the Member record to Accounts.isBlocked. Tier 3/4 contains no member-type branching.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effect is added in any tier. All changes are pure Tier 1/2 data and functions plus Tier 3 projections. The CLI and composition root are untouched.

evidence.quote: $"member {m} owes {money owed}; {blocked} blocked until it is below {money limit}"
| MemberBlocked of MemberId * BlockedActivity * owed: decimal * limit: decimal

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The 5.00/2.00/10.00 amounts are defined only in Policy.blockingBalance. The refusal message now uses the limit that Tier 2 put into the MemberBlocked error, so it no longer looks up the policy a second time and cannot drift from the guard. isBlocked and ensureNotBlocked both use the same Policy function.
